title: Design exercise: SAA-3.5-S06
scenario: Gorse Valley Bike Share collects position and battery readings from 45,000 bikes. Each bike reports about every 2.5 seconds at peak, so 18,000 records per second arrive, each about 400 bytes, and they must be captured continuously so a live map can show them within seconds. Nobody on the three-person platform team has run Apache Kafka, and the bikes' gateway software is written against the AWS SDKs. About 60 percent of the bikes are in one metro area. The same readings must also land in the data lake as large files within 5 minutes of capture, and analysts' dashboards filter by day and by city and must not scan the whole lake to answer one city for one day.
constraints: Do not claim live AWS experience
Finance wants a fixed, pre-agreed write capacity that is at most 20 percent above the computed minimum, not capacity that scales by itself
No additional staff may be hired to operate brokers or patch servers
Lake files should be large (tens of megabytes), not one object per reading

rubric.label: Write capacity covers the 18,000 records per second peak (arithmetic shown from both the record rate and the byte rate), stays within 20 percent above the computed minimum, and the record shows that the 60 percent concentration in one metro area cannot push any single unit of that capacity past its documented write limit
Lake files are large yet arrive within 5 minutes of capture, and a query for one city on one day reads only that slice of the lake

constraint_reason: Mapped as design_exercise to complete skill coverage when no dedicated live lab step exists
